findings.title: Graph extraction cannot support the promised analysis
findings.description:
The flow extracts project metadata, layers, tour, and selected nodes, but not `edges[]`; the output nevertheless promises dependency observations and entry points. The graph contract also does not establish that languages, frameworks, and dependencies are present in the fields being extracted. Grepping sections of JSON is not a reliable way to preserve object boundaries or resolve node IDs across formatting variants.

Specify structured extraction and the evidence needed for each output claim. Where the graph lacks that evidence, mark the result unknown rather than presenting an inferred dependency or entry point as fact.

findings.title: Staleness detection will routinely mischaracterize the graph
findings.description:
Comparing `meta.json`’s analyzed commit directly to `HEAD` misses uncommitted source changes, while committing the generated graph and metadata itself advances `HEAD` and makes a fresh graph appear stale. Commit distance also cannot always be calculated: the recorded commit may be unavailable in a shallow clone or on a divergent history.

Define how dirty source files, unavailable or divergent commits, and commits containing only graph artifacts are reported. Provenance should distinguish “current,” “drift detected,” and “freshness unknown,” rather than equating a commit mismatch with codebase drift.

findings.title: Repeated comprehension runs can overwrite the protected concept
findings.description:
Every run writes the same `000-concept.{project}.md`, yet its `User-Provided Concept` section must remain verbatim and may already contain human-authored material. The design specifies neither existing-concept detection nor a safe update or refusal policy. Analysis files receive new indices, but the concept does not.

Define behavior for an existing concept: preserve its protected section, avoid silently replacing other human edits, and make the proposed changes distinguishable from a new draft.

findings.title: The overview’s source and presentation rules conflict
findings.description:
With no concept, the inputs section allows purpose to come from an interview, while the translation rules require every claim to trace to an input artifact and the design goal calls the document derived rather than authored. The schema still requires problem, audience, and approach, whose listed sources are the missing concept. It also requires YAML frontmatter while saying frontmatter “never appear[s].”

Choose whether interview responses are permitted evidence, define how they are recorded and attributed, and specify explicit unknowns for unavailable fields. Clarify that frontmatter is present in the markdown artifact even if excluded from a client rendering.

findings.title: Status translation can overstate progress
findings.description:
The example translates “status draft” to “in progress,” although a draft plan is not evidence that implementation has begun. The example also uses `draft`, which the output conventions say the frontmatter gate rejects. The checked-in initiative plan combines checkboxes with status fields—for example, initiative 100 is checked but marked `in_progress`—so the overview needs a defined authority when signals differ.

Specify status precedence and a representation for ambiguous or unsupported progress; do not turn document maturity into implementation progress.

findings.title: New analysis artifacts collide with audit discovery
findings.description:
The proposed overview and comprehension filenames match the existing audit harness’s broad `*-analysis.*.md` glob in `src/squadron/metrology/audit.py`. `find_audit_file` selects the newest matching file, not necessarily a tech-debt audit. If another analysis artifact is written during an audit, the harness can select it and fail on its missing findings block instead of capturing the audit.

Make audit discovery identify the audit output specifically, and cover concurrent or intervening analysis writes. Merely reusing `docType: analysis` does not preserve the existing consumer’s assumptions.

findings.title: Index overflow is declared without a collision policy
findings.description:
The architecture says to use remaining 900-band slots beyond 949 while also acknowledging that the band is heavily used and subdivisions may need revision. It does not define how to select an index across document types and existing files, what happens when the range is exhausted, or how simultaneous runs avoid selecting the same slot. Declaring overflow sanctioned here does not update the project naming convention.

Define an allocation and collision policy consistent with the convention, including exhaustion and existing-file behavior, before directing both capabilities to consume the shared range.

findings.title: Dispatcher and pack upgrades can be out of sync
findings.description:
The dispatcher is installed under `sq`, while the skill is copied separately into the `analysis` prefix. Existing users can therefore update the dispatcher without updating the pack, or update the pack while retaining an older dispatcher. In particular, an installed analysis pack can lack `understand` even though the dispatcher advertises it.

Specify upgrade instructions and distinguish “pack absent” from “pack installed but skill missing,” including the remedy to reinstall or update the pack. Test the version-skew paths as well as a fresh install.

findings.title: Graph and metadata failures have no defined boundary
findings.description:
The design handles a missing graph but not malformed JSON, missing or changed fields, unresolved node references, absent metadata, or an upstream version changing the graph shape. Because the plugin is independently maintained, treating a partial extraction as a complete structural picture risks producing confident planning artifacts from incomplete data.

Define the minimum supported contract and fail or mark affected outputs unknown when it is not met. Include representative upstream-format fixtures, including partial and malformed inputs, rather than relying on the stated v2.8.1 shape alone.
